signalslinkep:usageinfo-signalslinkep-ti: SignalsLink.EP - Cooperation between the Signals and Electrical Progressive mods
signalslinkep:usageinfo-signalslinkep-te:
SignalsLink.EP
Extends the Signals mod with components that work with the Electrical Progressive mod.

If you want to turn an electrical circuit on and off with a signal, the EP switch will serve you. It is useful wherever a machine should run only when there is a reason.
If you need to know the state of the electrical network, use the EP meter. Based on the input signal it reports battery charge, production and consumption balance, or cable load, so you can start backup sources or disconnect consumers before the cable burns.
signalslinkep:block-handbooktext-epswitc:
Signal-controlled switch. Allows switching the flow of electric current on or off.
Connectors
Input — if there is a signal on it, the switch is on. If there is no signal on it, the switch is off.
signalslinkep:block-handbooktext-epmeter:
Allows obtaining information about the state of the electrical network to which the meter is connected. What it measures is determined by the signal on the input.
What the meter reports
Input 1 — battery charge. The output signal shows the charge state of batteries in the network. 0 - batteries are empty, 15 - batteries are fully charged.
Input 2 — production/consumption balance. Values 1-7: more is consumed than produced, 8: consumption=production, 9-15: production exceeds consumption.
Input 3 — current in the cable. The output signal shows the current in the cables at the block the meter is connected to. Values 0-12 represent current from 0 to the cable's maximum capacity. 13-15 represent cable overload (likely already smoldering and will burn soon).
Other signal — the output is signal 0.
